title: CLAUDE.md — spikeyglass
text: spikeyglass implements Bayesian Spike--Slab Joint Graphical Lasso (SSJGL) Li, McCormick & Clark (2019, ICML). method estimates multiple related Gaussian precision matrices (inverse covariance) across K groups simultaneously, using EM algorithm spike--slab priors adaptive, edge-specific penalization. Paper: Li et al. (2019) “Bayesian Joint Spike--Slab Graphical Lasso” (PMC7845917) Reference code: github.com/richardli/SSJGL Sibling package: github.com/mljaniczek/multiGGMr (Peterson et al. 2015, Bayesian GGM MRF priors)

what: Algorithm: EM with dynamic posterior exploration
title: CLAUDE.md — spikeyglass
text: Outer loop: Iterate decreasing ladder spike variance v0s warm-starting steps (dynamic posterior exploration, Section 3.3 paper). Smaller v0 → stronger shrinkage unlikely edges. E-step (gete() / gete.doubly()): Compute posterior probabilities edge inclusion P(delta=1) (doubly) similarity P(xi=1). Produces adaptive penalty weights d = (1-prob)/v0 + prob/v1 M-step. Uses log-sum-exp trick numerical stability. M-step (JGL.adaptive() + admm.iters.adaptive()): ADMM-based Joint Graphical Lasso matrix-valued lambda1/lambda2 penalties (edge-specific weights E-step). Theta update via eigendecomposition, Z update via JGL’s flsa2/dsgl. Pi update: Beta posterior mode: pi_delta = (+ sum_edges(prob1) - 1) / (+ b + n_edges - 2). Missing data: Optional conditional MVN imputation EM iteration (getmissing()).

title: CLAUDE.md — spikeyglass
text: Fused (penalty="fused"): Penalizes pairwise differences |Theta_k - Theta_l| across groups. Encourages similar precision matrices. Group (penalty="group"): Penalizes L2 norm sqrt(sum_k Theta_k^2) across groups. Encourages shared sparsity pattern.

what: Why v0 = 0.01 is a good default
title: Parameter exploration: understanding the v0 ladder
text: analysis illustrates several properties v0 = 0.01 (step 3): Well-calibrated probabilities: posterior probabilities neither near 0 (aggressive v0 values) diffuse (weak v0 values). means edges >50% probability genuinely supported data. Natural noise boundary: spike SD = 0.1, model treats partial correlations weaker ~0.1 noise. standardized data sensible — partial correlations 0.1 typically meaningfully different zero. Stable edge selection: graph structure step 3 typically stable — shrinkage (smaller v0) removes edges rarely adds . remaining edges robust. Short warm-suffices: EM v0 = 0.01 converges well just 2 warm-steps (v0 = 0.1, 0.03). full 10-step ladder useful exploration needed routine fitting.

title: Using spike-and-slab joint graphical lasso
text: spikeyglass package implements Bayesian Spike--Slab Joint Graphical Lasso (SSJGL) Li et al. (2019). method estimates multiple related precision matrices (inverse covariance matrices) across K groups simultaneously, encouraging shared sparsity structure allowing group-specific differences. Key features: Adaptive penalization: spike--slab priors automatically determine edge-specific penalty weights Two penalty types: fused (penalizes pairwise differences) group (penalizes L2 norm across groups) Posterior edge probabilities: edge gets posterior inclusion probability P(delta = 1), enabling principled edge selection Missing data handling: built-imputation via conditional MVN

E-step produces adaptive weights multiply value, effective penalty edge-specific. method relatively insensitive absolute value lambda1 (Li et al., 2019); matters ratio lambda1/v0. Guidance: Normalized data (normalize = TRUE): use 0.01–0.1 Raw data moderate variance: use 0.5–1 p >> n settings: use smaller values (0.01) lambda2 Scalar (matrix) base penalty cross-group similarity term. Controls borrowing strength across groups: lambda2 = 0: cross-group borrowing (separate estimation) lambda2 = lambda1: equal weight sparsity similarity lambda2 > lambda1: encourage similar graphs across groups lambda2 < lambda1: allow groups differ v1 Numeric slab variance parameter.
